learning_objective: 💼 Learn how to turn scientific lab discoveries into real-world products, patents, and successful startup businesses!

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: जैव-उद्यमिता (बायोलॉजी के ज्ञान से व्यवसाय शुरू करना)
पेटेंट (आविष्कारक को अपनी खोज पर मिलने वाला कानूनी एकाधिकार)
वेंचर कैपिटल (स्टार्टअप को मिलने वाला बड़ा निवेश/फंडिंग)
इनक्यूबेटर (वह संस्था जो नई कंपनियों को लैब, सलाह और सुविधाएँ देती है)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A scientist-turned-businessperson. They identify a problem (like a crop disease or a human illness), find a biological solution in the lab, and create a company to manufacture and sell that solution to the world.

Before selling an idea, you must protect it so others don't steal it. A patent gives you exclusive rights to make, use, and sell your invention for a limited time (usually 20 years). In biotech, you can patent genes, engineered microbes, and drugs.

Biotech is expensive and takes years to show profit. Startups raise money through Angel Investors (rich individuals) or Venture Capitalists (firms investing in high-risk, high-reward tech) to fund their clinical trials and manufacturing.

Most startups don't have money to build a multi-million dollar lab. Bio-incubators (like those supported by BIRAC in India) provide startups with shared lab space, expensive equipment, legal advice, and mentorship.

Unlike a software app, if a biotech drug fails, people could die. Therefore, bioentrepreneurs face strict regulations. They must pass Phase I, II, and III clinical trials and get approval from agencies (like the FDA or CDSCO) before selling.

fun_activity.title: 👩‍🔬 The Indian Biotech Pioneer
fun_activity.instructions: Read the story of Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw. She started 'Biocon' in 1978 in the garage of her rented house in Bengaluru with just Rs. 10,000. She extracted enzymes from papayas. Today, Biocon is India's largest biopharmaceutical company, proving that great businesses start with small ideas!

exam_tips: 📌 BIRAC (Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council) is a critical term. It's an Indian government enterprise set up to foster innovation and support biotech startups.
📌 Know the standard duration of a patent (usually 20 years from the date of filing).
📌 Be able to explain why biotech startups have a higher risk and longer 'gestation period' (time before making profit) compared to IT startups—mainly due to R&D and clinical trials.
quick_recap: ⭐ 'Biopiracy' is the unethical commercial exploitation of biological materials or traditional knowledge without compensation.
⭐ Angel investors fund startups in their earliest stages, while Venture Capitalists come in later with massive funding for scaling up.
⭐ Patents, Trademarks, and Copyrights fall under the umbrella of Intellectual Property Rights (IPR).
